result.title: Learning When to Think Aloud in Latent Reasoning
result.summary: Latent Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning improves efficiency by shifting intermediate computation into continuous hidden states. However, fully latent methods often struggle on precision-critical tasks such as mathematical reasoning, while existing hybrid approaches retain substantial token-generation overhead. We introduce VITAL, an importance-guided hybrid reasoning framework that selectively verbalizes informative tokens as reasoning anchors while keeping most computation latent. A lightweight gating head dynamically selects between explicit token generation and direct hidden-state feedback. VITAL constructs hybrid trajectories from explicit CoT using token- importance estimation and trains the model through curriculum-based supervised training, followed by reinforcement learning with a reward that balances correctness and conciseness. Experiments show that VITAL consistently out- performs existing fully latent reasoning methods, achieving relative average accuracy gains of 9.6% on GPT-2 and 5.1% on Llama-3.2-1B at comparable reasoning lengths. Compared with hybrid baselines, VITAL achieves higher reasoning accuracy with substantially shorter reasoning trajectories on Qwen3-1.7B.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VITAL 混合推理框架：用轻量 gating head 动态决定何时把隐状态转为显式 token 作为「推理锚点」，其余计算保持 latent；轨迹由显式 CoT 的 token 重要性估计构造，经课程式监督训练与兼顾正确性与简洁性的强化学习训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 THINK 边界问题——何处值得外显、何处留在 latent，可作为「选择性 verbalize」的收益/成本对照；但实验仅在 GPT-2、Llama-3.2-1B、Qwen3-1.7B 小模型上，gating 依据与长度泛化仍需核查。
